bib.title: EVA: Exploring the Limits of Masked Visual Representation Learning at Scale

SOURCE: "EVA: Exploring the Limits of Masked Visual Representation Learning at Scale", Yuxin Fang, Wen Wang, Binhui Xie, Quan Sun, Ledell Wu, Xinggang Wang, Tiejun Huang, Xinlong Wang, Yue Cao (BAAI, HUST, ZJU, BIT). Preprint: the PDF is stamped "arXiv:2211.07636v2 [cs.CV] 5 Dec 2022" and names no venue. The filename's 2023 is not supported by the PDF.

COVERAGE: I read all 77,209 of 77,209 chars: the body, all appendix tables (12–19) and the references (skimmed for origins). There is only one figure caption (Fig. 1, p1). Everything else is tables.

CLAIMS
- claim: The pretext task is to reconstruct masked-out CLIP vision features from the visible patches, with no tokenization. It uses block-wise masking at 40%, targets from the OpenAI CLIP-L/14 vision tower (224px) and a negative cosine similarity loss.
  number: 40%
  setup: EVA pre-training. Output is layer-normed, then linearly projected to the CLIP dimension.
  quote: "we use block-wise masking with a masking ratio of 40% following [5, 70, 104]. The target for MIM pre-training is from the publicly available OpenAI CLIP-L/14 vision tower trained on 224×224 pixel images [73]... We use negative cosine similarity as the loss function."
  where: p3, §2.2
- claim: The model is a vanilla ViT-g of about 1.0B parameters.
  number: 1011M; patch 14×14, 40 layers, hidden 1408, MLP 6144, 16 heads
  setup: Table 3a. Pre-training uses no relative positional embeddings and no layer-scale.
  quote: "14×14 40 1408 6144 16 1011M"
  where: p3, Table 3a

LIMITS:
- The authors say the regression pretext task is not theirs ("not originally proposed by us"; MVP and MILAN). What they contribute is scaling it up.
- "Public data only" needs the caveat above: the target is CLIP trained on 400M pairs.
- No masking-ratio ablation. 40% is borrowed from BEiT. The target ablations use ViT-B only, and there is no scaling curve across model sizes.
- They concede EVA does not "solve" LVIS: rare 48.3 vs common 55.5 vs frequent 57.4 mask AP. ADE20K is below BEiT-3, which they put down to a weakened head.
- Their own Table 5 says absolute accuracies are "not directly comparable" across models.
- The "emergent" LVIS claim rests on one model scale.
- Every SOTA claim is timestamped Nov 10, 2022, so it has dated.
- EVA-CLIP is not tested as a VLM encoder (BLIP-2 is not mentioned) and there is no retrieval result in the paper; the 35-benchmark evaluation is linked out only.

BUILDS ON: MVP [109] (Wei et al., 2022) and MILAN [44] (Hou et al., 2022) for the masked CLIP-feature target. BEiT (Bao et al., 2021), BEiT v2 (Peng et al., 2022) and BEiT-3 (Wang et al., 2022) for block masking and the codebase. ViT (Dosovitskiy et al., ICLR 2021) and ViT-g shape (Zhai et al., CVPR 2022). CLIP (Radford et al., ICML 2021). FD (Wei et al., 2022) for the distillation baseline. ViTDet (Li et al., 2022). ViT-Adapter (Chen et al., 2022) and Mask2Former (Cheng et al., 2021). OpenCLIP (Ilharco et al., 2021). MAE (He et al., 2021).

CODE: none in the paper. It points to https://github.com/baaivision/EVA (p1).

FIGURES: Fig. 1 (p1), "An illustration of this work. We find with sufficient image data (30M) and compute (150 epochs), simply regressing the masked out image-text aligned vision features (i.e., CLIP features) scales up well (to 1.0B parameters)..." It is a one-glance pipeline: CLIP teacher → MIM-pretrained EVA → downstream tasks, including initializing a larger CLIP, which is the link to BLIP-2. For teaching, Table 3 (architecture, data, compute) and Table 10a (CLIP training cost comparison) are more useful than the figure.

PROBLEMS:
- The extraction is clean apart from spacing ("EV A", "2242" meaning 224²).
- The paper contradicts itself in three places:
  (1) EVA-CLIP IN-1K zero-shot is 78.5 in Tables 1, 10b and 11, but the text says "is 78.2%".
  (2) Samples seen are "11B" in the Table 10a body, but the caption says "fewer image-text pairs (7B v.s. 12B / 32B)".
  (3) The 12-benchmark average is 75.7 in the Table 10b body, but the caption says "(72.7% top-1 accuracy)".
  Cite the table values and note the conflict.
- COCO val box AP for EVA appears as 64.2 in Table 7 and 64.1 in Table 8b, which differ in TTA/setup.
